answer.origin: Fox News Digital article by Amanda Macias, published 2026-07-01. Corning CEO Wendell Weeks and planning supervisor Emily Capek are directly quoted; Fox reports the Corning–NVIDIA project and Wistron’s Texas operations.
answer.note: Weeks said Corning was in its fastest growth period and would probably double in size over the coming years, with almost all new hires in advanced manufacturing and a significant part in the United States (incoming; statement and publication date 2026-07-01; event horizon: “over the coming years”). This is a forecast about Corning, not NVIDIA. Capek said demand for Corning glass optical fiber was supporting AI demand (item:e4; 2026-07-01), while Fox reported Corning was ramping up optical-fiber production amid rising AI-infrastructure demand (item:e1). Fox also reported that Corning and NVIDIA partnered earlier in 2026 on three advanced optical-manufacturing facilities in North Carolina and Texas, expected to create more than 3,000 jobs and expand Corning’s U.S. optical-manufacturing capacity tenfold; no completion date was given (items:e2, e5, e6). Separately, Fox reported Wistron was establishing Texas AI-supercomputer manufacturing operations for NVIDIA (item:e7). Together, these reports support the view that NVIDIA’s AI infrastructure expansion is associated with activity among suppliers and manufacturing partners, including potential optical-fiber supply and U.S. manufacturing capacity. They do not establish NVIDIA’s direct orders, purchase amounts, or the realized timing and scale of the projects; the Corning growth and capacity figures describe Corning, not NVIDIA.
limitations: The article gives no NVIDIA order or purchase value, contract terms, or specific allocation of Corning’s planned capacity to NVIDIA.
The Corning facilities’ completion schedule and whether the reported job and tenfold-capacity expectations are achieved are not stated.
The article does not provide a timeline or quantified production output for Wistron’s Texas operations.
follow_up: Check NVIDIA and Corning announcements and subsequent filings for project milestones, facility completion timing, and any disclosed supply commitments or order values.
Check Corning updates for realized U.S. optical-manufacturing capacity, hiring, and whether the three facilities meet the reported expectations.
Check NVIDIA and Wistron disclosures for the start and scale of Texas AI-supercomputer manufacturing operations.
